Why a tag-stripped verbatim text conforms to the edición oficial: the Diario Oficial is the official edition (the Imprenta Nacional publishes it by law), the stored text is cut from the Diario Oficial PDF itself by pdftotext, nothing is reworded, translated, corrected or re-ordered (running page headers and page numbers of the edition are dropped, the law's words and sequence are those of the edition), and each record names the edition number and carries the PDF sha256. The qualifier 'siempre y cuando no esté prohibido' is read as a prohibition of law or of the issuing body; the Imprenta terms quoted in terms_quote restrict the contents of the Imprenta website (its own texts, images and design, 'propiedad de la Imprenta Nacional o de terceros autorizados'), not the laws and decrees that the State issues and the Imprenta only prints. The page is a Wix page; the text hashed includes the navigation. DECISION FOR VARUN: this pass rests on Ley 23 de 1982 art. 41, which is a permission to reproduce tied to fidelity to the official edition, not an exclusion from copyright, and which is silent on modification and on commercial use. Reading against pass: the Imprenta terms say reproduction, distribution or modification is prohibited without prior authorisation, and art. 41 ends 'siempre y cuando no esté prohibido'. If that reading is taken the verdict becomes permission requested and the four Diario Oficial records (co-ley-1931-2018, co-ley-1819-2016-art221-223, co-ley-2277-2022-art47-49, co-decreto-969-2026) are removed. Text recipe in SOURCES.md ## Colombia. The Diario search page on svrpubindc.imprenta.gov.co carries no terms text of its own; the terms page is the one linked from the Imprenta home page.
